page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine provisioned with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. The instance runs on an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, structured as 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 33 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, AES-NI, and BMI2.

Hardware allocation lacks bundled local storage and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating network-attached storage and distinct network routing configurations for standard operations. The platform contains no hardware accelerators or discrete GPUs. Memory subsystem throughput benchmarks reach 205.55 GB/s for small cached blocks and 27.03 GB/s for uncached reads, paired with a PassMark memory score of 1978.71.

Benchmark outcomes show modest computational capabilities across standard benchmarks. The server registered a single-core Geekbench score of 1147.0 and a multi-core score of 2501.0, accompanied by a PassMark CPU score of 4258.56. In execution tests, it completed single-threaded gzip compression at 23.85 GB/s, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression yielded 16.02 GB/s. Application evaluations measured static web serving throughput at 3.73 GB/s and Redis SET operations at 3.61 million operations per second.

Given its balanced ratio and dedicated compute allocation, the instance provides steady execution for mid-tier application hosting, standard web servers, intermediate build environments, and microservices. Heavy vector computing, machine learning training, and local I/O intensive databases face bottlenecks due to baseline computational scores and lack of bundled local NVMe storage.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual instance configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16 GB of memory on an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz. The architecture presents 2 physical cores supporting simultaneous multithreading, 33 MB of L3 cache, and instruction extensions including AVX-512 and AES. The instance does not include bundled local storage or discrete graphics acceleration, depending on networked block storage for persistent data. Performance benchmarks indicate modest throughput, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 2501.0, 3.61 million Redis SET operations per second, and 3.73 GB/s static web serving throughput. Its memory bandwidth achieves 27.03 GB/s on large uncached reads. The balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory configuration delivers qualitative cost efficiency for predictable enterprise workloads, containerized services, and web application backends that do not demand high-performance acceleration or intensive local input-output pipelines.

16 GB system memory adhering to a standard 1:4 core-to-memory configuration
